title: Which Entries Are Netted to Find What Stands Short
content:
Which entries are netted to find what stands short on a Keyturn Host Payout Account turns on how the account settles and on what caused the shortfall.

| How the account settles | Money charged back by a guest standing on the account | Entries netted |
|---|---|---|
| Swept as each trip completes | Yes | Every entry ever booked to it |
| Swept as each trip completes | No | The entries booked in the twelve months up to that day |
| Any other rhythm | Any | Only the entries booked in the month up to that day |

Whichever stretch is netted, what stands short is taken as a positive sum where that netting falls below nothing and as nothing where it does not, and is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## Points of judgement

**An account swept as each trip completes with money charged back by a guest standing on it.** The first row governs and the whole history of the account is netted.

**The same account with no chargeback money standing on it.** The second row governs and the stretch is the twelve months up to that day.

**An account settling on any other rhythm.** The third row governs whatever the chargebacks show, and only the month up to that day is netted.

## On hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical account whose entries over its whole life net to 700.00 USD below nothing, whose entries in the twelve months up to that day net to 300.00 USD below nothing, and whose entries in the month up to that day net to 200.00 USD above nothing. What stands short is 700.00 USD in the first row, 300.00 USD in the second and nothing at all in the third, since a netting at or above nothing leaves nothing standing short.
